newsitem.title: FRANCE: Air France Europe Sept cargo traffic down.
newsitem.headline: Air France Europe Sept cargo traffic down.

text.p: Air France Europe said it handled 33,700 tonnes of freight in the first eight months of 1996, a decrease of 13.2 percent on the same period last year.

"The decline in tonnage is directly related to a reduction in capacity, the airline having replaced Airbus 300 and 330 passenger aircraft, which could carry up to six tonnes of freight with Airbus 320s and 319s whose bellyholds offer only one to two tonnes maximum," Air France Europe's marketing manager for freight, Gerard Plassat, told Reuters.
As a result, the airline had re-focused its cargo traffic strategy on small packages and express shipments and was carrying fewer heavy category loads, Plassat said.
January-August turnover totalled 125.2 million French francs, down 4.2 percent on 1995 levels.
"Turnover has not decreased in the same proportions as tonnage because we have succeeded in improving our yields. In simple terms, we've earned more from a smaller volume of traffic," Plassat said.
Traffic obtained from Air France Europe's door-to-door express product, Lasair, rose by 3.7 percent on the first eight months of 1996, to 7,900 shipments.
"Turnover from Lasair, in the period in question, was up 22 percent on January-August 1995 and now accounts for nine to ten percent of global turnover, a rise of 2.5 percentage points."
Lasair offers half-day deadlines for packages with an average weight of 100 kilos using the airline's network of around 400 daily flights.

The performance of the French carrier's airport-to-airport and airport-to-door express product, Airporte, which is geared to shipments with a maximum unit weight of 30 kilos, had stagnated on 1995 levels as some major customers, such as DHL Worldwide Express, had introduced their own dedicated all-cargo flights, Plassat added.

Air France Europe, formerly Air Inter, is to launch a new express product next week following the start of its new "shuttle" services between Paris-Orly and Marseille, Toulouse and Nice. - Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
